params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# WHAT THE CURATOR OFFERS THE MODEL IT SERVES (GH #892, OR-KY-G1). The curator
# answers the collector's menu question like any tools hive: its tools in
# `schemas[]` (provider-neutral `{name, description, parameters}`), its sections
# of the sidecar block in `sidecar[]` (`{section, required, schema,
# instruction}`), filed under the answerer `curator` -- the collector merges
# every answerer's half into one menu and one block contract (#529/#606), so
# there is no second place a contract is composed.
#
# ONE LIST, one entry per tool or section, and each strand that gives the
# curator something to offer writes its entry into it: an entry with a `name`
# is a tool, an entry with a `section` is a section. The cell that answers the
# `in_schemas` lane is named `schemas` in every hive (tree rule R4, GH #548).
#
# A section answered here comes back to the curator on `in_section` (the
# splitter cuts it, OR-KY-G2); a tool answered here is called through the
# dispatcher like any other.
WINDOW = ("Every earlier block of your window that is not your own answer starts with"
          " its id, like [#0123456789ab]. Under `release`, list the ids of blocks you no"
          " longer need: each shrinks to one line at the next rebuild of your window and"
          " stays readable in full with history_read. Under `pin`, list the ids you must"
          " keep in full. Write the section only when it applies.")

# THE HISTORY TOOLS (GH #893): what `./history` serves, the model's own wall.
# A pure literal, read with `ast` by the locks that hold its property names to
# what that cell reads (`ARGS` there) and its names to the menu the parents
# expect; spliced into `CURATOR_OFFER` below at the strand's anchor.
HISTORY_SCHEMAS = [
    {"name": "history_search",
     "description": (
         "Search your own earlier turns -- every session you had, the running"
         " turn included -- for a text. Deterministic,"
         " no model involved. Hits come newest first, each with its block id"
         " (`#` and 12 hex digits, as your window shows them), turn, time, kind"
         " and an excerpt; read a whole block with history_read. Your own earlier"
         " history_* calls and their answers are left out. A search stops once"
         " `limit` hits are found (`stopped_at_limit`), or cut short by its scan or"
         " time budget (`truncated_scan`, `cut_by`)."),
     "parameters": {
         "type": "object",
         "properties": {
             "query": {"type": "string",
                       "description": "what to find; in `regex` mode a regular"
                                      " expression of at most 200 characters"},
             "mode": {"type": "string", "enum": ["phrase", "exact", "regex"],
                      "description": "`phrase` (default): these words in this order,"
                                     " any case, any spacing; `exact`: this text,"
                                     " case-sensitive; `regex`: a regular expression"},
             "since": {"type": "string",
                       "description": "ISO-8601 time; only turns at or after it"},
             "until": {"type": "string",
                       "description": "ISO-8601 time; only turns at or before it"
                                      " (a bare date is the whole day)"},
             "kinds": {"type": "array",
                       "items": {"type": "string",
                                 "enum": ["user", "assistant", "peer", "advice",
                                          "delegation", "tool_call", "tool_result",
                                          "recall", "brief"]},
                       "description": "only blocks of these kinds"},
             "limit": {"type": "integer",
                       "description": "hits to show, 1 to 20 (default 8)"},
             "context": {"type": "integer",
                         "description": "neighbouring blocks of the same session"
                                        " to show beside each hit, 0 to 2 (default 0)"}},
         "required": ["query"]}},
    {"name": "history_read",
     "description": (
         "Read blocks of your own earlier turns in full, never shortened: one block"
         " by its id (`#` and 12 hex digits, as your window and history_search show"
         " it), or every block of a turn range. A block your window only names by"
         " its id is read whole this way. A read larger than the budget is refused"
         " with `too_large` and its size; ask for less. A turn range leaves out your"
         " own history_* calls and their answers (`skipped_history`); read one by"
         " its id."),
     "parameters": {
         "type": "object",
         "properties": {
             "id": {"type": "string",
                    "description": "the block id, e.g. `#3f2a9c01b7de`"},
             "from_turn": {"type": "string",
                           "description": "the first turn of a range (a turn id as"
                                          " history_search or history_outline name it)"},
             "to_turn": {"type": "string",
                         "description": "the last turn of the range; one of the two"
                                        " alone reads that one turn"}},
         "required": []}},
    {"name": "history_outline",
     "description": (
         "An outline of your own earlier turns: the sessions with their first and"
         " last turn and time and how many turns they had, and the topics each"
         " session opened and closed."),
     "parameters": {
         "type": "object",
         "properties": {
             "since": {"type": "string",
                       "description": "ISO-8601 time; only sessions active at or after it"}},
         "required": []}},
]

CURATOR_OFFER = [
    # -- the window section: TRIM through the answer's sidecar (GH #892) -------
    {"section": "window", "required": False,
     "schema": {"type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "release": {"type": "array",
                                "items": {"type": "string", "description": "#<id>"}},
                    "pin": {"type": "array",
                            "items": {"type": "string", "description": "#<id>"}}}},
     "instruction": WINDOW},
    # -- history_search, history_read, history_outline (GH #893) --------------
    *HISTORY_SCHEMAS,

    # -- the gap section (GH #895) --------------------------------------------
    # What the model was unsure of or missed in an answer: `./push` looks it up
    # after the answer has left, never before it, and a find opens the next
    # round of the session as an addendum (in a duplex call it is also said).
    {"section": "gap", "required": False,
     "schema": {"type": "string",
                "description": "what you were unsure of or missed, in a few words"},
     "instruction": ("write what you were unsure about or missed; it will be"
                     " looked up after this answer")},
]

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc.get("body") or {}
asked = body.get("tools")
names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)] if isinstance(asked, list) else []

tools = [e for e in CURATOR_OFFER if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("name")]
sections = [e for e in CURATOR_OFFER if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("section")]
have = [str(t["name"]) for t in tools]
if "*" in names:
    schemas = list(tools)
else:
    schemas = [t for t in tools if str(t["name"]) in names]
seen, unknown = set(), []
for n in names:
    if n == "*" or n in seen or n in have:
        continue
    seen.add(n)
    unknown.append(n)

header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown,
    "sidecar": sections, "messages": []}))

description.purpose: What the curator offers the model it serves, as a menu answer (GH #892, OR-KY-G1): its own tools in `schemas[]` -- the model's own wall, `history_search`, `history_read`, `history_outline` (GH #893), served by `./history` -- and its sections of the sidecar block in `sidecar[]` -- the `window` section, through which the model releases and pins blocks of its window by their short ids, and the `gap` section, what it was unsure of or missed, looked up after the answer (GH #895). One list, `CURATOR_OFFER`, holds every entry: a `name` is a tool, a `section` is a section. The asking collector merges this answer with every other answerer's under the answerer `curator` and composes menu and block contract as it always does.
description.use_when: Reached on the curator's `in_schemas` lane only, which the parent draws from its collector's `schemas` question; answered on `tool_schemas`, which the parent draws back into that collector as `in_menu` with `context.tool_answerer` `curator`.
description.not_in_scope: No tool call is answered here: a tool this cell declares is called through the dispatcher like any other, and a section it offers comes back to the curator on `in_section` after the splitter cut it. No fence and no frame -- the collector composes the contract.
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: the declared tools the question named (`*` = all of them), provider-neutral. unknown[]: every other name it was handed, verbatim and deduplicated -- another answerer serves those -- with hop.error_code `tool_unknown` when that list is non-empty. sidecar[]: every section of the list, on every answer, including one handed no `tools` slot at all.
description.consumes_meaning: body.tools: the names the asking collector declares it uses. Optional: the sections are the same without it.
examples: {"tools":["*"]} -> every declared tool, no unknown, the sections
{"tools":["web_search"]} -> no schema, unknown ["web_search"], hop.error_code `tool_unknown`, the sections
